rv.q: The character’s worldly awareness and general streetwise-ness increases with age – and one of the reasons why this story is so intense is its longitudinal nature: there’s a lot of story to get through in ninety minutes.

This is the single period in the play where there is uncomplicated joy as the friendship develops. It’s the boy who tells her, with naïve enthusiasm, about all the benefits this factory will bring to their lives in Bhopal. But as she narrates it in hindsight, the girl has realised it’s far from the truth.
Halder does find moments of humour, drawing laughter from the audience as ‘She’ is a young girl full of hope, before switching to the darkest moments of grief as her story runs its course.
